title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Water
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: The multistate water-utility PLC campaign has reached at least 12 states, and federal agencies name Iranian-affiliated actors
items.content_text: Water and wastewater utilities in at least 12 states have reported cyberattacks on their operational technology since late July. Actors reached internet-exposed Rockwell and Allen-Bradley MicroLogix controllers, changed device IP addresses and set unauthorised passwords, locking operators out of monitoring and control. More than 30 Minnesota community water systems were affected, Clayton County, Georgia issued a boil-water advisory after a pump-station failure, and Michigan, South Dakota, New Jersey and Alabama have all confirmed incidents. Joint advisory AA26-097A assesses that Iranian-affiliated CyberAv3ngers, tied to the IRGC Cyber Electronic Command, is behind the activity. No CVE was exploited: the entry path is controllers reachable from the internet with default, shared or absent credentials. Officials say drinking-water safety has not been compromised at any affected utility.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA/FBI advisory AA26-097A and state disclosures — via The Record, Axios and SecurityWeek
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Campaign since 26–27 Jul 2026; latest confirmations 12–14 Aug 2026

items.title: The campaign produced real operational consequences: a pressure drop, a boil-water advisory, a lift-station incident
items.content_text: Beyond locked-out controllers, the campaign has caused documented physical effects. Clayton County Water Authority in Georgia, which serves about 300,000 customers in the Atlanta area, reported cyber activity that caused a water-pressure drop and forced a boil-water advisory. Minnesota IT Services reported coordinated activity against more than 30 community water systems statewide beginning 28 July, with Plymouth, South St. Paul, Maple Plain and Braham confirming operational impacts. A wastewater lift station in Rapid City, South Dakota was also affected, and Michigan and New Jersey have reported incidents. In several cases utilities lost remote control of pumps, valves and pressure and reverted to manual operation. Officials maintain that treated-water safety was not compromised.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Axios and CBS News, citing state utilities and federal officials

items.title: AA26-097A now covers Schneider and Siemens PLCs too, and adds detection guidance for tampered code modules
items.content_text: The joint advisory behind this campaign, AA26-097A, was issued on 7 April by the FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE, US Cyber Command’s Cyber National Mission Force and Treasury, and updated on 22 July. The update matters for water operators in two ways. First, the observed manufacturer scope expanded beyond Rockwell Automation to include Schneider Electric and Siemens PLCs, so a utility that replaced its MicroLogix fleet is not automatically out of scope. Second, the agencies added guidance for detecting malicious changes inside reusable code modules used within Rockwell PLC programs — a reminder that the risk is not only lockout but altered logic. Reported techniques include Dropbear SSH remote access, project-file exfiltration and HMI or SCADA data manipulation that disables shutdown and alarm logic.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Issued 7 Apr 2026, updated 22 Jul 2026; campaign ongoing through 14 Aug 2026

items.title: 4,407 Rockwell controllers are still reachable from the internet — 22 of them in cities already hit
items.content_text: A Shodan-based scan by Forescout Vedere Labs on 3 August found 4,407 internet-facing Rockwell Automation and Allen-Bradley programmable logic controllers worldwide, 2,844 of them in the United States. Twenty-two sit in cities where water and wastewater utilities have reported attacks since late July, and 19 of those 22 appear vulnerable to CVE-2017-16740, a buffer overflow in MicroLogix 1400 controllers that Rockwell patched nine years ago. Forescout attributes much of the exposure to small and mid-sized utilities connecting controllers to cellular routers for remote monitoring, which keeps staffing costs down but frequently leaves EtherNet/IP or Modbus TCP answering from the open internet. Total exposure is down 47 percent from a 2020 peak of 7,814, which is progress and still far too many.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Forescout Vedere Labs — via The Hacker News and CyberScoop

items.title: Gunra ransomware is exploiting known VPN and firewall flaws, and utilities are named among its victims
items.content_text: The FBI, CISA, DoD Cyber Crime Center, NSA, US Secret Service and the Republic of Korea’s National Police Agency published #StopRansomware advisory AA26-222A on Gunra, a double-extortion operation derived from leaked Conti source that moved to an affiliate model in early 2026. Its victim base explicitly includes utilities, alongside healthcare, finance, manufacturing, transport and government. Initial access comes from exposed edge infrastructure — VPN gateways, firewalls and RDP — including the Fortinet FortiOS and FortiProxy authentication-bypass flaws CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472. For a water utility, this is a different failure mode from the PLC campaign: it will not lock you out of a controller, but it will encrypt billing, SCADA historians and the engineering workstations you need to recover.

items.title: A suspected China-nexus actor is mass-exploiting a patched vCenter flaw, with ransomware behind it
items.content_text: Exploitation of CVE-2026-59310, a directory-traversal flaw in Broadcom VMware vCenter rated CVSS 9.8 and patched on 29 July, has been attributed to a suspected China-nexus actor. German incident-response firm QUIRSO counted roughly 361 victim IP addresses across 47 countries, 343 of them appearing between 3 and 5 August, and assesses with moderate confidence that a Chinese-speaking operator is behind it. The chain establishes persistence through cron jobs, systemd units and reverse_ssh, drops a Linux backdoor, and in some cases deploys Babuk-derived ransomware. Mid-sized utilities that consolidated SCADA servers, historians and HMI virtual machines onto a single VMware cluster should treat this as an availability risk to operations, not just an IT patching item.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: The Hacker News, reporting QUIRSO research

items.title: Dragos logged 1,140 industrial ransomware incidents in Q2 — none of them touched a control system
items.content_text: Dragos recorded 1,140 ransomware incidents affecting industrial organisations in the second quarter of 2026, up 12 percent on Q1, with 514 in North America. Manufacturing took 747; organisations supporting ICS environments took 117. Notably, Dragos observed no ransomware operator directly manipulating an industrial control system during the quarter. Disruption came from encrypted enterprise IT and precautionary shutdowns of virtualisation and shared infrastructure. For water utilities this is a useful counterweight to the PLC campaign: the nation-state activity in the headlines does reach controllers, but the far more common ransomware scenario stops at the business network and still takes the plant down, because billing, procurement, lab systems and remote support all live there.

items.title: Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway has an unauthenticated root command-injection flaw rated CVSS 10.0, with water named in scope
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-225-02 describes CVE-2026-19188, an operating-system command-injection vulnerability in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway rated CVSS 10.0. The Net Check feature reachable via the /setting endpoint passes unsanitised input to the cmdPing Socket.io event, allowing arbitrary commands to run as root. CISA lists Water and Wastewater Systems, Energy and Critical Manufacturing among the affected sectors, and Haiwell has released fixed firmware. This class of low-cost cloud HMI gateway is exactly what small utilities and their contractors deploy on lift stations, booster stations and remote wells so the system can be checked from a phone — the same deployment pattern Forescout blames for most PLC exposure. No public exploitation has been reported to CISA.

items.title: Fifteen ICS advisories landed in one day — WaterISAC has the sector-filtered roundup
items.content_text: CISA released 15 industrial control system advisories on 13 August, following three on 11 August and two on 4 August. WaterISAC republished the batch with sector filtering, which is the practical way for a small utility to read it: most of these products will not be in your plant, and the ones that are deserve a change ticket rather than a skim. Affected vendors in the batch include Johnson Controls, Hitachi Energy and ANDRITZ, alongside earlier August advisories covering Schneider Electric remote terminal units, Mitsubishi Electric CPU modules and Delta Electronics engineering tools. None of the items carries reported active exploitation, so this is routine patch-and-monitor work rather than an emergency — but it is the work that keeps the emergency list short.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: WaterISAC roundup of CISA ICS advisories

items.title: An actively exploited Cisco ASA and FTD flaw joins the KEV catalogue
items.content_text: CISA added three vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 11 August: CVE-2026-20349, a heap inspection vulnerability in Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and Firepower Threat Defense; CVE-2026-68820 in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock; and CVE-2026-72898, a SQL injection flaw in Metabase. The Cisco entry is the one that reaches water utilities most directly, because ASA appliances are a common choice for the boundary between the business network and SCADA, and for terminating vendor remote access. KEV listing means exploitation is confirmed in the wild. Read alongside the Gunra advisory, the pattern for August is consistent: attackers are getting in through known flaws in perimeter appliances, not novel OT exploits.

items.title: August ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens ships ten advisories, led by a maximum-severity IoT2050 flaw
items.content_text: Siemens, Schneider Electric and Phoenix Contact published their August ICS Patch Tuesday advisories. Siemens issued ten, the most serious a maximum-severity missing-authentication vulnerability in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices that allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute code with elevated privileges. Water utilities running Siemens S7 controllers should read the full bundle rather than the headline, and Schneider Electric’s advisories are worth checking against Modicon and Saitel deployments — one covers faulty input validation in Saitel DR and DP remote terminal units that could allow denial of service. No exploitation has been reported for any of these, so schedule them into the normal maintenance window rather than treating them as an interrupt.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: SecurityWeek, summarising Siemens ProductCERT, Schneider Electric and Phoenix Contact advisories

items.title: The Water Cyber Shield Act would give EPA assessment authority and $300 million a year
items.content_text: Senators Amy Klobuchar and Adam Schiff introduced the Water Cyber Shield Act of 2026 on 12 August, directly in response to the attacks on water systems across roughly 12 states. The bill amends the Safe Drinking Water Act and the Clean Water Act to give EPA the authorities it needs as sector risk management agency: expanded power to conduct cybersecurity assessments and to require corrective action when significant vulnerabilities are found. It would also authorise an additional $300 million a year through the Drinking Water and Clean Water State Revolving Funds for cybersecurity improvements. It is an introduced bill, not law, and previous attempts to give EPA mandatory authority over water cybersecurity have not survived the legislative process — but the funding line is the part small utilities should track.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Sen. Klobuchar news release — corroborated by The Record
